My land is 3.8 mu and I've been running wheat-maize rotation on it for as long as I can remember. Same piece of ground, same system. It works. I'm not changing it.

**Wheat (October planting):** I'll plant winter wheat on the full 3.8 mu after the maize comes off in late September. I'll use Jimai 22 — local seed station sells it, my neighbors use it, I've used it for years. Good yield, stands well against lodging. Before planting I'll do rotary tillage to turn in the maize stubble. I'll apply base fertilizer at planting — compound fertilizer plus some urea. Then topdress urea again at jointing in March. Three irrigations: winter water in November to help the crop overwinter, jointing water in April, and grain-filling water around May. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and hit the crop once more with fungicide and insecticide around heading. Powdery mildew and aphids are the usual problems here.

**Maize (June planting):** Right after wheat harvest in early June I'll direct seed maize — no tillage, just go straight in. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed. Better yield than the old stuff. Apply fertilizer at planting, topdress at the big bell stage. Two irrigations if the summer rains are short — one at seeding if it's dry, one at tasseling. Spray herbicide right after seeding and watch for corn borer and armyworm in August.

Two people in the house — my wife and I can handle 3.8 mu without hired help except maybe at wheat harvest when I'll hire the combine.
